question.text: When a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> electric heater is immersed in a gas for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> in a constant volume container with adiabatic walls, the temperature of the gas rises by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The heat capacity of the given gas is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>JK</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> (Nearest integer)

solution.text:
Heat capacity = Heat absorbed  change in temperature 

1 Watt = 1 Joule per second

Hence, heat absorbed =60×100J

Change in temperature =5°C

Heat capacity=60×100 J5

=1200JK-1
